newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Singapore announces technical assistance program.
newsitem.headline: Singapore announces technical assistance program.

text.p: Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong of Singapore on Tuesday announced a technical assistance programme to help train officials from developing countries in urban planning, transportation and other areas.
He made the announcement in a speech to a U.N. Earth Summit reviewing progress made since the 1992 Rio de Janeiro conference on the environment.
"No country has all the answers. Singapore learns all the time from others, their successes and mistakes," Goh said.

Cooperation was necessary to solve global problems of sustainable development, he said, adding: "It is in this spirit that I now announce the Singapore Technical Assistance Programme for Sustainable Development (STAPSD) for developing countries.

"This is a modest programme aimed at sharing our experience with others from the developing world. It focuses on training of officials in areas like urban planning, management of parks and transportation."
Referring to Singapore, Goh said that what a country with a population of three million could do globally was only a drop in the ocean.
But its programme was offered "as a tangible token of our seriousness to promote greater cooperation in sustainable development."
He hoped the initiative would encourage the larger and more prosperous countries of the developed world to "fulfil their commitments and join us in what must be a global endeavour."
